key_facts: Airplane cabins are pressurized to a lower pressure than sea level, causing gas inside sealed containers to expand.
Deep-sea environments have extreme high pressure that has the opposite effect on sealed containers.

2026-10-02-1.script: Ever wonder why your soda can feels rock solid on an airplane? It all comes down to cabin pressure physics at thirty thousand feet. Planes mimic an altitude of about eight thousand feet, not sea level. That lower air pressure outside causes the trapped gas inside to expand. The metal walls stretch, turning your drink into a ticking time bomb. Deep sea vessels face the exact opposite crushing problem underwater. So pressure builds when you fly, which begs the ultimate question... What happens to a marshmallow inside a vacuum chamber?
